title: Q/K normalization + M-RoPE
mechanism: Extend Q/K/gate kernel to apply rotary embedding. Pool is standalone rotary pass. Preserve Gemma RMSNorm semantics.

title: Q/K normalization + M-RoPE + KV-cache write
mechanism: Alternative to F03: eliminate rotary/cache intermediates. Pool is rotary and cache kernels. Preserve current KV precision, scaling, layout, and write ordering.

title: Full-attention output/segment reduction + sigmoid gate
mechanism: Prefill: gate in attention output epilogue. Decode: gate in reduce_segments final store. Pool is gate-only kernel. Does not eliminate segment reduction.

title: Linear input GEMM epilogue emits final QKV/Z/B/A layout
mechanism: Remove standalone layout pass using projection epilogue or a consumer reading original layout. Two separate projections must complete before combined consumers run.

title: Linear convolution consumes projection layout and emits split Q/K/V
mechanism: Fuse layout/split work around FlyDSL prefill conv or decode conv update. Pool is the two layout kernels; convolution time is retained. Preserve state update and Z/B/A branches.

title: Prefill conv epilogue + Q/K L2 norm + gating/split
mechanism: Normalize Q/K and emit gates from conv output; row reductions and gate inputs require a compatible tile. Pool is split/gating/L2 passes, not convolution arithmetic.

title: Prefill gating + chunk-local cumulative sum
mechanism: Compute gating and chunk scan in one kernel. Retain the scan dependency; pool is separate cumsum time.
overlap: F08; T04 may redesign this boundary

title: Decode delta update consumes packed conv output
mechanism: Alternative consumer-side split elimination: update reads conv layout directly. Preserve speculative state/rollback semantics.

title: Linear attention output + gated RMSNorm
mechanism: Prefill chunk output or decode recurrence epilogue applies existing gated RMSNorm; cross-channel reduction can raise registers and reduce occupancy. Pool is standalone norm.

title: KKT solve + recompute W/U
mechanism: Pool is BOTH kernels, not removable overhead. Savings percentages model faster combined execution; triangular solve/tiling/global dependencies may prevent useful fusion.

title: Chunk state recurrence + output calculation
mechanism: Pool is BOTH compute kernels. Requires dependency-aware persistent/chunk scheduling; do not treat recurrent computation as removable.

title: Gated RMSNorm + attention output projection
mechanism: Alternative to F11: projection consumes normalization inline. Norm reduction and GEMM tiling may require recomputation or synchronization.

title: Shared-expert down projection + shared/routed output combination
mechanism: Fuse combination into the last completed producer or consumer; need both expert paths and correct gate. Pool is combination pass.

title: Shared-expert gate/up GEMM + SiLU-and-multiply
mechanism: GEMM epilogue produces activated shared-expert intermediate. Pool is separate activation; preserve both gate/up halves.
overlap: Shared-expert overlap can hide some savings

title: TopK routing + MoE sorting/workspace passes
mechanism: Reduce routing/sorting passes and initialization through a coordinated routing backend. Pool is sorting only. Global histogram/prefix dependencies can still require multiple launches.
overlap: F18,F19; do not simply delete global scans

title: MXFP4 quantization + token permutation
mechanism: Quantize directly to expert-consumption layout. Pool is permutation passes only; quantization retained. Reuse scales without excess token duplication.

title: First expert GEMM epilogue + intermediate FP4 quantization/permutation
mechanism: Pool uses half of quantization time (one of two calls per layer) plus second permutation. Requires correct per-group scales and output packing; no extra SiLU saving because moe1 already fuses it.

title: MoE weighted reduction + shared-expert combination
mechanism: Use moe_reduction_kernel_0 final stores to combine shared expert. Pool is combination only; weighted reduction retained.

title: Second expert GEMM + weighted expert-output reduction
mechanism: Avoid materializing expert outputs or use tile-owned accumulation. Global expert-to-token reduction, atomics, determinism and precision can erase gains. Pool is standalone reduction.
overlap: T05; F20 can follow only if dependencies allow

title: Input/post-attention normalization + GEMM or quantization consumer
mechanism: Alternative placement to F01. Reduction dimensions and shared consumers can force recomputation. Pool is normalization, not GEMM time.

title: Decode router TopK + existing fused MoE
mechanism: Integrate routing only if expert selection can feed persistent/block scheduling without duplicate work. Decode experts already run as one fused aiter::fmoe kernel.
overlap: T02; do not re-count already fused expert stages

title: Merge QKV/Z and B/A input projections
mechanism: Pool is BOTH projection GEMMs, not removable overhead. Concatenate compatible weights and use one GEMM or grouped launch, with custom output layout. Shape/precision compatibility and changed tiling determine whether it helps.

title: Decode convolution state update + gated delta recurrence
mechanism: Pool is BOTH compute kernels. Conv and recurrent states have different layouts; verify query-order dependencies, speculative state snapshots and rollback before considering a persistent fused kernel.

title: Router projection epilogue + TopK/softmax
mechanism: Alternative to F23: router GEMM emits top-k selections. Global expert-dimension reduction may not fit the GEMM epilogue; exact routing and scoring semantics must be preserved. Pool is TopK only.

title: Tune existing decode fused MXFP4 MoE
mechanism: Tune persistent scheduling, expert tiling, weight loads and occupancy for recorded batch shape; pool is whole existing fused MoE.

title: Tune decode full attention and split count
mechanism: Tune NUM_SEGMENTS_PER_SEQ=128, query tiling, and reduction; fewer segments trades occupancy for reduction cost. Pool is attention+reduction. Keep BF16 Q and FP8 KV; NVIDIA FP8-Q path is not a precision-equivalent target.

title: Tune prefill GDN state kernel
mechanism: Pool is recurrence computation. AMD is already faster than NVIDIA for this named stage in these traces. Tune only after larger bottlenecks.

title: Tune prefill MXFP4 expert GEMMs
mechanism: Pool is two expert GEMMs on unaffected prefill passes. Tune tile sizes, traffic and expert imbalance; malformed duration records excluded.

title: Tune input/output/shared/router GEMMs
mechanism: Pool includes all target-step GEMMs including logits. Use per-module shapes; compare alternative kernels within AMD. Improvements here are not the same as deleting GEMMs.

title: Overlap shared expert with routed MoE
mechanism: Pool is shared-expert work that may be hidden behind routed MoE, not deleted. AMD target work is on one stream; NVIDIA uses auxiliary streams. Resource contention and join dependencies limit overlap.
overlap: F16 and shared-expert GEMM tuning affect same pool
